_comment: Sample input for rubric.py. This belief is mostly defensible but its falsifier search is weak.
claim: For a breadth-first survey, parallel multi-agent retrieval beats a single agent.
falsifier: If a single agent with the same token budget matched multi-agent coverage/quality, the claim fails.

falsifier_search.found: Cognition argues single-threaded is better for interdependent work, but that is a different task type.
falsifier_search.notes: Did not run a controlled same-budget comparison myself.

evidence.provenance_report: Anthropic primary + MAST peer-reviewed + STORM academic; blog echoes collapsed.

steelman.opposing_view: Cognition: multi-agent is fragile; writes must stay single-threaded.
steelman.why_unconvinced: Their case is interdependent/write-heavy coding; a survey is breadth-first/read-heavy, the regime where multi-agent is validated.
